summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and AuroraGrid. Discussed AuroraGrid's managed GPU cloud offerings, integration opportunities (private deployments, marketplace, referral partnership), performance benchmarking, security/compliance requirements, and next steps for a technical deep dive and partner agreement.
transcript:
00:00 Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on the partnerships team, with Samir our solutions engineer. Could you quick intro yourselves?
00:06 Maya Chen: Yeah hi, Maya here, Head of ML at AuroraGrid. We run the managed GPU cloud and lot of enterprise customers.
00:11 Rafael Torres: Rafael, cloud architecture, I look after networking and infra.
00:14 Priya Gupta: Priya, partnerships, curious about commercial models.
00:17 Samir Patel: Great, appreciate you all. Quick agenda: partner intro, what AuroraGrid offers, where Redwood fits, perf/security checks, and next steps. Sound good?
00:25 Maya Chen: Yep sounds good. Rafael do you wanna kick off with a bit of what AuroraGrid provides?
00:29 Rafael Torres: Sure. We provide GPU-backed VMs and managed Kubernetes clusters, specialized for large model workloads. We have racks of A100s and custom Ampere variants. We do single-tenant racks for larger customers, and marketplace for smaller teams.
00:45 Lena Ortiz: Nice. A few of our partners are similar; curious how you differentiate on performance and network egress for KV cache-heavy workloads.
00:53 Rafael Torres: Our local NVLink pods reduce cross-node hops, so for KV cache heavy, sticky scheduling keeps the cache local. We also offer a low-latency fabric between racks — it's a paid add-on but helps with long context.
01:03 Samir Patel: That helps. On Redwood's side we run a serving runtime that benefits from low-latency interconnects for KV cache and batching. Typical ask: can we get perf numbers for sustained 8k token context with a 30ms per-token SLO?
01:18 Maya Chen: 30ms is tight. We usually aim for 40-60ms depending on model size. We can try to tune.
01:24 Lena Ortiz: That's exactly the kind of thing our SEs would validate in a benchmark. Samir, can you outline what we'd need to run a quick smoke benchmark on AuroraGrid?
01:31 Samir Patel: Sure. Ideally we need a test VM with the same model bits or a compatible quantized variant, GPU metrics access (nvidia-smi logs), network latency to the control plane, and a sample prompt set representative of customer workloads. Also access to a bucket for logs and an SSH jumpbox for instrumentation.
01:45 Rafael Torres: We can provide a jumpbox and bucket, but we'll need a short IAA for access. We have an internal security review but for a partner POC we can expedite.
01:53 Priya Gupta: On commercials — we have a partner program with revenue share tiers and referrals. Curious how Redwood typically structures dedicated deployments vs marketplace integrations.
02:02 Lena Ortiz: For dedicated we do reserved capacity contracts — committed monthly/annual. For marketplace integrations we support self-serve model selection and a referral fee or listing fee depending on lead flow. We can share a partner guide.
02:14 Maya Chen: Security — SOC2 is important for many of our customers. Do you require SOC2 for Private deployments?
02:19 Samir Patel: For Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and audit logs; we are SOC2 compliant and can share the report under NDA. Also SAML/SSO and RBAC are supported.
02:27 Rafael Torres: Good. For on-prem or private tenancy, how does Redwood handle kernel / runtime installation? Is it containerized? We're worried about version drift.
02:35 Samir Patel: We ship a containerized runtime with a control plane connector. For fully air-gapped installs we can provide an offline package and an ops-runbook. Kernel-level optimizations are packaged as binaries and we keep a compatibility matrix.
02:47 Priya Gupta: Integration opportunities — we want to list AuroraGrid as a recommended infra partner for customers who need dedicated racks. What do you typically expect from a partner in terms of co-marketing?
02:57 Lena Ortiz: Typically a joint case study, a reference architecture doc, and a couple of webinars. We can allocate co-marketing credits based on deal milestones.
03:06 Maya Chen: Makes sense. Back to perf — Samir, what's the fastest path to validate 8x A100 equivalence?
03:12 Samir Patel: Realistically, run a short 2-3 day benchmark with a 50-100k token workload, run both a 4k and 8k context test, and measure p99 latencies. If you can provide a small fleet we can spin the runtime and compare throughput and token cost. For cost modeling we'd need utilization patterns.
03:30 Rafael Torres: We can provision a pod for that. We'll need to coordinate on NV switches and whether to enable your preferred kernel flags.
03:36 Samir Patel: We'll send a recommended config — kernel flags, CUDA/CUDNN versions, and a runbook.
03:42 Maya Chen: On billing - if we list AuroraGrid in Redwood marketplace, who bills the customer? AuroraGrid or Redwood?
03:48 Lena Ortiz: For marketplace we support both models. If AuroraGrid wants to bill directly we can do referral-based listing; if you'd like Redwood to resell, we handle billing and pass through to you with settlement terms. We can discuss margins.
03:59 Priya Gupta: Good. Any regulatory constraints? We have customers in EU and APAC who ask for data residency. How does Redwood support region pinning?
04:07 Samir Patel: We support region pinning and can route requests to designated regions. For private deployments you control where inference runs; for hosted, we have region options and compliance packages.
04:16 Maya Chen: Excellent. Let's talk about a pilot scope: initial target is 1) benchmark for perf/cost, 2) security review for SOC2/KMS, 3) partner listing trial in marketplace. Timeline ideally 4-6 weeks. Thoughts?
04:28 Lena Ortiz: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to get the partner guide and SOW over in 2 business days and schedule the tech deep dive next week.
04:34 Rafael Torres: One more question — for KV cache warm starts across replicas, how does Redwood reconcile cache eviction when autoscaling? We see cache thrash concerns.
04:43 Samir Patel: We support sticky sessions and session-aware routing; we also have a warm-backfill policy that pre-populates KV on scale-ups for critical models. There is tradeoff with cost vs cold-start latency. We'll include our recommended autoscaling knobs in the runbook.
04:56 Maya Chen: Great. Also curious about quantization support — we do a lot of int8 inference. Does Redwood support quantized model variants?
05:02 Samir Patel: Yes, we support int8 and int4 in various runtimes, and can fallback to fp16 if needed. Our compiler selects kernels based on model and hardware. We'll need to know the model variant to suggest the best profile.
05:12 Priya Gupta: From the partnership ops side, what's the simplest first step? A short pilot and then a co-marketing plan?
05:18 Lena Ortiz: Exactly. Pilot + joint go-to-market plan. We'll propose a 6-week pilot: weeks 1-2 setup and infra, week 3 run benchmarks, weeks 4-5 optimize, week 6 review and case study planning.
05:30 Rafael Torres: That timeline looks doable. We'll prioritize the jumpbox and infra diagrams.
05:34 Maya Chen: Ok I can share prompt sets and example traffic profiles by EOD tomorrow.
05:38 Lena Ortiz: Perfect. We'll follow up with the partner guide, SOW template, and a calendar invite for the technical deep dive.
05:44 Priya Gupta: That works. Any blockers from Redwood side for the POC?
05:48 Samir Patel: Just access and a short IAA for the jumpbox. Also we'd like GPU telemetry and permission to run stress tests during a scheduled window.
05:57 Rafael Torres: We'll do a maintenance window, coordinate times.
06:01 Lena Ortiz: Awesome. Let's recap next steps...
06:04 Lena Ortiz: Action items: Lena send deck & SOW by Friday; Samir schedule deep dive; Rafael share infra; Maya share prompt set. Priya will coordinate BD intro.
06:15 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to it.
06:18 Lena Ortiz: Thanks all, talk soon.
06:20 [call ends]
notes: Customer is interested in both marketplace listing and dedicated rack referrals; security/compliance looks compatible but will need SOC2 report and IAA; pilot timeline ~4-6 weeks; key technical check is p99 latency at 8k context and KV cache behaviour during autoscale.
questions: What are AuroraGrid's typical utilization patterns (spiky vs steady)?
Can AuroraGrid provide GPU telemetry for benchmarks?
Which quantized model variants are most common for your customers?
